title: Normal ramification filtration
statement: Let $B$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field $L$ and residue characteristic $p>0$, with $p$ prime [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-pc-field-extension]. Every finite field extension $M/L$ embeds in a finite normal extension $N/L$ which has a tower $L=L^0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq L^r=N$. Write $B^j$ for the integral closure of $B$ in $L^j$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Each nonidentity step is of one of these types: (a) purely inseparable of degree $p$, meaning characteristic $p$ and every $x$ has $x^p$ in the preceding field; (b) Galois of degree $p$; (c) cyclic Galois of degree prime to $p$, with ramification index prime to $p$ and separable residue field extension; (d) unramified, meaning $\mathfrak m_{B^j}B^{j+1}=\mathfrak m_{B^{j+1}}$ and the residue field extension is finite separable. Galois means normal and separable, normal means splitting of every irreducible polynomial having a root, and cyclic refers to the field automorphism group [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. In (c), the ramification index $e$ means $\mathfrak m_{B^j}B^{j+1}=\mathfrak m_{B^{j+1}}^e$. These types are stable under base change, for any such tower and not only the one constructed: let $A\to B'$ be an injective local map of complete DVRs with fraction fields $K\subseteq E^0$ and residue field of $B'$ of characteristic $p$, let $E^0\subseteq E^1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq E^s$ be finite field extensions each nonidentity step of which is of type (a), (b), (c) or (d) with respect to the integral closures of $B'$ in the $E^j$, let $K'/K$ be finite, and choose a field factor $E^s_1$ of $(E^s\otimes_K K')_{\mathrm{red}}$. Then the subfields $E^j_1\subseteq E^s_1$ generated by the images of $E^j$ and $K'$ form, after deleting identity steps, a tower of length at most $s$ each step of which is of one of the four types (a)-(d) with respect to the integral closures of $B'$ in the $E^j_1$, and all these integral closures are complete DVRs. Tensor product and reduction have their usual algebra meanings, reduction being quotient by nilpotents [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 09F8, lemma-special-case, proof paragraphs 2-4 (normal closure, inertia filtration, and branchwise base-change of the filtration), using Tag 09EE, lemma-galois-inertia, and Tag 09EH, lemma-inertial-invariants-unramified.

proof.text: For each complete DVR $D$ encountered below and finite extension $T/\operatorname{Frac}(D)$, let $S=\operatorname{IntCl}_T(D)$. The DVR definition makes $D$ a nonfield local PID. Thus $D$ is Noetherian and normal by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] and has dimension one by [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one]. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata], $D$ is Nagata. Its zero ideal is prime, so the definitions [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring, def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] give that $S$ is a finite $D$-module, without a separability assumption. It is a domain, being a subring of $T$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product] makes $S$ local and complete. By [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-local-dvr] there is a maximal ideal $q$ of $S$ over $\mathfrak m_D$, and $S_q$ is a DVR with fraction field $T$ and maximal ideal contracting to $\mathfrak m_D$. Since $S$ is local, this $q$ is its unique maximal ideal and every denominator outside $q$ is a unit, so $S=S_q$. Therefore $S$ is a finite complete DVR, and $D\to S$ is local. This argument applies separately to every finite field extension used below.

source.place: Tags 032W (lemma-Noetherian-complete-local-Nagata), 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local), 00PD and 00PH; the first proof paragraph of More on Algebra Tag 09F8.

proof.text: Choose a finite normal extension $N/L$ containing $M$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-extension-in-finite-normal-extension]. By [lem-weil-pbc-normal-extension-purely-inseparable-then-galois] there is $L\subseteq F\subseteq N$ with $F/L$ purely inseparable and $N/F$ Galois. Both subextensions are finite, since an intermediate field is a vector subspace of $N$ over $L$. In characteristic zero $F=L$ by the definition of pure inseparability. In positive characteristic, the embedding $B\subseteq L$ shows $\operatorname{char}(L)=p$: a field of positive characteristic has that same characteristic in any nonzero residue field of a subring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-pth-root-tower] to $F/L$ to obtain its degree-$p$ steps. For a step $H(\alpha)/H$ with $\alpha^p\in H$, every rational expression in $\alpha$ has its $p$th power in $H$, so it is type (a). Step 1, with $D=B$, makes the closures in all these intermediate fields finite complete DVRs with local inclusions.

source.place: Tag 09F8, lemma-special-case, second and third proof paragraphs; Fields 09DT and 030M; Fields 09HI

proof.text: Put $R=\operatorname{IntCl}_F(B)$ and $C=\operatorname{IntCl}_N(B)$. Transitivity of integral elements [lem-sfb-integral-element-tower-descent] shows that $C$ is also the closure of $R$ in $N$: integrality over $B$ implies integrality over $R$, and the reverse implication uses $R/B$ integral. These rings are complete DVRs by step 1. Let $G=\operatorname{Aut}_F(N)$. Every element of $G$ preserves $C$, because it preserves monic equations over $R$, and hence preserves its unique maximal ideal. Thus the decomposition group is all of $G$. Apply [lem-exc-finite-dvr-tame-inertia] to $R,N/F,C$ and its maximal ideal: the inertia group $I$ has a normal subgroup $P$, of $p$-power order, and $I/P$ is cyclic of order prime to $p$. Put $U=N^I$, $V=N^P$. Their integral closures are complete DVRs by step 1.

source.place: Tag 09F8, third proof paragraph; Tag 09EE, lemma-galois-inertia

proof.text: The fixed ring $C^G$ is $R$: [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] identifies the fixed fraction field with $F$, and the elements of $C\cap F$ and of $R$ are, by their definitions, exactly the elements of $F$ integral over $B$. Likewise $C^I=C\cap U$ is the integral closure of $B$ in $U$, by the defining monic-equation condition. Apply [lem-dl-a1-finite-group-inertia-invariants-etale] to $G$ acting on $C$ at its maximal ideal. It makes $\operatorname{Spec}(C^I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ etale on a neighbourhood of the closed point. Since $C^I$ is local, any open containing its closed point is the entire spectrum. Apply [lem-sbc-etale-trait-stalk] at that point: a uniformizer of $R$ generates the maximal ideal of $C^I$, and hence the index is one. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable] to this etale map: its residue extension is finite separable. Therefore $U/F$ is type (d), unless it is the identity.

source.place: Tag 09EH, lemma-inertial-invariants-unramified; its generalization Tag 0BST in pione.tex

proof.text: By [lem-wf-finite-field-action-fixed-degree], $N/U$ is Galois of degree $|I|$ and $N/V$ is Galois of degree $|P|$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field], the full automorphism groups of these finite Galois extensions have exactly these degrees as their orders. Since they contain $I$ and $P$, respectively, they equal those subgroups. Apply [lem-per-finite-galois-normal-fixed-quotient] to $N/U$ and $P\triangleleft I$. It identifies $\operatorname{Aut}_U(V)$ with $I/P$, so $V/U$ is cyclic Galois. The same finite-Galois cardinality theorem gives its degree $n=|I/P|$, prime to $p$. By [lem-exc-dvr-galois-degree-data], its unique normalized DVR branch has $ef=n$. Thus both $e$ and $f$ are prime to $p$. Its residue extension is normal by [lem-exc-dvr-residue-normal-action]. For that characteristic-$p$ residue extension [lem-exc-normal-field-degree-factors] writes $f=s p^b$, where $p^b$ is the degree over the subfield of separable elements. Coprimality forces $b=0$, so every residue element is separable. This is type (c) if $V\ne U$.

source.place: Tag 09F8, third proof paragraph; Tag 09EE; Tags 09EB, 09ED, 09HS, 09HI

proof.text: If $P=1$, then $V=N$. Otherwise apply [lem-sfb-finite-p-group-normal-index-p] repeatedly, first to $P$ and then to each subgroup obtained, obtaining $P=P_0\supset P_1\supset\cdots\supset P_a=1$, with $P_{i+1}$ normal in $P_i$ of index $p$. The order falls by a factor $p$ at each step, so the iteration terminates. Set $H_i=N^{P_i}$. By [lem-wf-finite-field-action-fixed-degree], $N/H_i$ is Galois of degree $|P_i|$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field], its full automorphism group has that same order, and hence equals its subgroup $P_i$; applying [lem-per-finite-galois-normal-fixed-quotient] to $P_{i+1}\triangleleft P_i$ gives $H_{i+1}/H_i$ Galois with group $P_i/P_{i+1}$, hence degree $p$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] again. These are type (b); no assertion that their residue extension is trivial is used. Concatenate $L\subseteq F$, $F\subseteq U$, $U\subseteq V=H_0$, and this last tower. Delete identities to get the first assertion.

source.place: Tag 09F8, third proof paragraph: refining the wild inertia p-group

proof.text: Now take the arbitrary tower and finite base change in the second assertion. Work inside the chosen top field factor $W=E^s_1$. All maps from the fields $E^j$ and $K\prime$ into $W$ are injective. Set $F_j=E^jK\prime\subseteq W$ and $C_j=\operatorname{IntCl}_{E^j}(B\prime)$, $D_j=\operatorname{IntCl}_{F_j}(B\prime)$. The image of $E^j\otimes_K K\prime$ in $W$ is a finite-dimensional $E^j$-algebra and a domain. A nonzero element acts injectively on this finite-dimensional vector space and therefore surjectively, so has an inverse in the image. Thus the image is already the field $F_j$; in particular $F_j/E^j$ is finite. Since $E^j/E^0$ and $F_j/E^j$ are finite, so is $F_j/E^0$ (products of finite spanning sets span). Step 1 with $D=B\prime$ makes all $C_j,D_j$ finite complete DVRs. By [lem-sfb-integral-element-tower-descent], $D_j$ is also the integral closure of $C_j$ in $F_j$, and $D_{j+1}$ is the closure of $D_j$ in $F_{j+1}$. The inclusions are therefore local by step 1 applied with those complete base DVRs and finite fraction-field extensions. Their residue characteristic is $p$, by the corrected hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 09F8, fourth proof paragraph: normalized base-change branches

proof.text: For a type (a) step $E^{j+1}/E^j$, every $p$th power of a rational expression in elements of $E^{j+1}$ and $F_j$ lies in $F_j$, so $F_{j+1}/F_j$ is purely inseparable of exponent at most one. Also its degree is at most $p$: the $p$ elements of an $E^j$-basis of $E^{j+1}$ span the image algebra over $F_j$, which is a field by the finite-dimensional-domain argument in the preceding step, and is exactly $F_{j+1}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-pth-root-tower] to this finite purely inseparable extension, and multiply the degrees of its steps using [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity]. Its degree is a power of $p$ between $1$ and $p$, hence either $1$ or $p$. In the latter case it is type (a); in the former case it is deleted.

source.place: Tag 09F8, fourth proof paragraph: persistence of case (a); Fields 09HI and 09G9

proof.text: For a type (b) step apply [lem-sfb-galois-compositum-restriction] with $k=E^j$, $K=E^{j+1}$, $F=F_j$ and ambient field $F_{j+1}$. The new step is Galois and its group injects into the group of order $p$. By [lem-exc-finite-group-cauchy] the old group has an element of order $p$, whose $p$ distinct powers exhaust its $p$ elements. Every nonidentity power is again a generator, since its exponent is invertible modulo $p$. Thus its subgroups are trivial or the entire group. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] the new degree is the order of its group, hence $1$ or $p$, so the surviving step is type (b). For a type (c) step the same restriction theorem gives a cyclic Galois group of order dividing the original prime-to-$p$ cyclic order (if the original generator has order $n$, the least positive exponent $d$ whose power belongs to the subgroup divides $n$ by Euclidean division; dividing any other such exponent by $d$ shows the subgroup consists of these powers and has order $n/d$). Thus its degree is prime to $p$.

source.place: Tag 09F8, fourth proof paragraph: Galois degrees and cyclicity under compositum

proof.text: For a type (c) step apply [lem-sfb-dvr-tame-unramified-compositum-permanence] to the local DVR inclusion $C_j\hookrightarrow D_j$ and the finite separable extension $E^{j+1}/E^j$. The original normalized extension is tame by the definition in the item. The compositum $F_{j+1}$ is a field factor of $E^{j+1}\otimes_{E^j}F_j$: the multiplication map is onto, by the finite-dimensional-domain argument of step 7. The theorem gives prime-to-$p$ ramification index and finite separable residue extension for its normalization over $D_j$, which is $D_{j+1}$ by step 7. With the cyclic Galois conclusion of step 9 this is type (c), unless the step is an identity.

source.place: Tag 09F8, fourth proof paragraph; Tag 0EXY, lemma-tame-goes-up (2). Only the type (c) step, whose fraction-field extension is Galois and hence separable.

proof.text: For a type (d) step put $Q=(E^{j+1}\otimes_{E^j}F_j)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure] with $A=C_j$, $B=C_{j+1}$, $P=F_j$: the map is injective local by step 7, and $F_j/E^j$ is finite. It gives $Q=\prod_\alpha Q_\alpha$ with field factors. Multiplication is onto $F_{j+1}$ by step 7 and kills nilpotents. A surjection from a finite product of fields to a field sends exactly one of the orthogonal coordinate idempotents to $1$ and the others to $0$; its restriction on that factor is an isomorphism. Thus one $Q_\alpha$ is the chosen compositum $F_{j+1}$. Write $S_\alpha=\operatorname{IntCl}_{Q_\alpha}(C_{j+1})$. Then $H=\operatorname{IntCl}_Q(C_{j+1})=\prod_\alpha S_\alpha$: projection of a monic equation proves one inclusion, and the product of monic annihilators for all coordinates annihilates their tuple, proving the other. Each $Q_\alpha/E^{j+1}$ is finite, as a quotient of the finite-dimensional tensor algebra; step 1 makes $S_\alpha$ a complete DVR. For the selected factor, $S_\alpha=D_{j+1}$ by the closure identification in step 7. Let $q$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak m_{D_{j+1}}$ under $H\twoheadrightarrow D_{j+1}$. This is maximal. In $H_q$ the selected idempotent is a unit and kills the other factors; the surviving denominators are units of $D_{j+1}$. Consequently $H_q=D_{j+1}$.

source.place: Tag 09EM, remark-construction (finite tensor field factors and normalized branches); Tag 09F8, branchwise base-change paragraph. The product and localization identifications are the displayed monic-equation and idempotent calculations.

proof.text: For this type (d) step apply [lem-sfb-dvr-index-one-separable-base-change] with $A=C_j$, $B=C_{j+1}$, $K=E^j$, $L=E^{j+1}$, $N=F_j$. Its hypotheses on $A\to B$ are exactly the old step: index one and separable residue extension; its finite-field hypothesis is $F_j/E^j$, proved in step 7. No separability of $E^{j+1}/E^j$ is required. In the notation of that lemma, $R=D_j$ by step 7, and $C=H$, $C_q=D_{j+1}$ by step 11. The lemma says $n=q\cap D_j$ is maximal, hence $n=\mathfrak m_{D_j}$ since $D_j$ is local, and $R_n=D_j$. Its equality $nC_q=qC_q$ is therefore $\mathfrak m_{D_j}D_{j+1}=\mathfrak m_{D_{j+1}}$, and its residue conclusion gives separability. This residue extension is finite as well: step 1 makes $D_{j+1}$ finite over $D_j$, and images of module generators span the residue field over $D_j/\mathfrak m_{D_j}$. Thus the surviving step is type (d), including when the old fraction-field extension is inseparable.

source.place: Tag 09EQ, lemma-formally-smooth-goes-up, using the index-one and separable-residue criterion Tag 09E7 and normalized branches of Tag 09EM; Tag 09F8 branchwise induction.

proof.text: The subfields $F_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_s$ are nested because their two sets of generators are nested, and their endpoint is $W$: the image of $E^s\otimes_K K\prime$ in its chosen field factor generates all of $W$. Remove a repeated field whenever $F_j=F_{j+1}$. Removing repetitions changes neither the maps nor the normalized rings for any remaining adjacent nonidentity step; the surviving steps are exactly the nonidentity steps already treated. There are at most $s$ of them. Step 7 has already proved completeness and the DVR property for every normalization.
